summary: The copy is careful, plain and almost free of A13 risk: the language lint holds, the pinned texts are intact, and most screens say what will happen and what is kept without judging. The main problems are consistency and a few misleading words. Two lines claim a benefit ("parts you want to sharpen", "help you stay sharp"); on the results, "SD" means both the scale unit and an estimate's uncertainty ("+0.88 (SD 0.60)"), and the same 90% quantity is an "interval" in the table but a "range" everywhere else. The drill-down shows internal facet ids ("Simple rt", "Linear eq", "Recip"), internal words "block" and "item" reach people, and the privacy notice people agree to still shows TODO(user) placeholders. Names drift between screens (Reaction time / Reaction Time; sequence / series; piece / cell; shape / object; squares / blocks), the session length is 30, 28 or 31 minutes depending on the screen, and the answer button is Confirm or Submit by item type. Every finding gives exact replacements and the e2e/script/test literals that would need updating.
coverage: Inventory: 1,569 user-facing strings with file:line, screen and kind (web/ux-review/findings/copy-inventory.json), from every copy module, inline Svelte text and aria-label/title/placeholder/alt values, save/parse errors, segment intros, axis names, notes builder modules (gated line texts tagged), and index.html, notes.html, rt-selftest.html (title, meta description, noscript); dev-only code (src/backend, src/dev, src/review, visual-gallery) excluded
Tour of all 50 product routes, Chromium desktop 1280 px light, page text + accessibility tree per route (test-results/ux-review/copy/tour)
Results with every disclosure open: one session (results-open) and two sessions (results-two, practice-adjusted wording)
A full ?fast=1 journey with practice questions, every interstitial and intro, down to the results (test-results/ux-review/copy/journey)
Evidence close-ups of the quoted strings (test-results/ux-review/copy/evidence)
Literal matches of every proposed change grepped in web/e2e/*.ts, web/scripts/*.ts, *.test.ts and snapshots

findings.title: Focus-session and break copy imply a training benefit ('sharpen', 'stay sharp')
findings.env: Chromium desktop 1280 px, light (vite preview of the shared _dist, ?fast=1 for the session routes)
findings.observed: web/src/reveal/copy.ts:131 FOCUS_TEXT: "Pick the parts you want to sharpen. A focus session takes about 20 minutes and only covers the parts you choose." (ready screen of a returning person and the results 'Coming back for more' section). web/src/session/copy.ts:172 BREAK_OFFER_TEXT: "You have been working for about 30 minutes. A short break can help you stay sharp. The clock pauses while you rest." 'Sharpen' reads as the focus session improving a skill, which the product explicitly corrects for (practice-adjusted estimates, §7.8), and 'help you stay sharp' is a performance-benefit claim.
findings.expected: A focus session is described as measuring the chosen parts more precisely; the break is offered without claiming an effect. No copy claims a benefit beyond the A22 sentence.
findings.suggestion: Exact replacements. reveal/copy.ts:131 FOCUS_TEXT → "Pick the parts you want measured more precisely. A focus session takes about 20 minutes and covers only the parts you choose." session/copy.ts:172 BREAK_OFFER_TEXT → "You have been working for about 30 minutes. You can take a short break now: the clock pauses while you rest." Literal matches in e2e/*.ts, scripts/*.ts, *.test.ts: none (tests import the constants).

findings.title: 'SD' means two different things on the results: the scale unit and an estimate's uncertainty
findings.env: Chromium desktop 1280 px, light (vite preview of the shared _dist, ?fast=1 for the session routes)
findings.observed: web/src/viz/BarTable.svelte:68 renders the estimate as "+0.88 (SD 0.60)" in the column headed "Estimate (SD)", and web/src/viz/copy.ts:33 UNCERTAINTY_CAPTION says "The light band spans ±1 SD". In both, SD is the estimate's own uncertainty, while everywhere else (ring labels '+1 SD', RING_CAPTION, 'Compared with 0 SD', peaks, card) SD is the unit of the scale. A reader sees '(SD 0.60)' as a second score and reads the band as one ring wide.
findings.expected: One meaning for SD (the scale unit). The uncertainty of an estimate is shown as ± a number and called uncertainty.
findings.suggestion: BarTable.svelte:68 `(SD {row.sd.toFixed(2)})` → `± {row.sd.toFixed(2)}` (cell reads "+0.88 ± 0.60"). viz/copy.ts:53 TABLE_CAPTION → "Estimates by skill, in SD units on a provisional scale, each ± its uncertainty, with 90% ranges." viz/copy.ts:33 UNCERTAINTY_CAPTION → "The solid line is the most likely profile. The light band shows each estimate ± its uncertainty, and the soft edge around the line fades out across each 90% range: the darker the shading, the more plausible that value. Whiskers show 90% ranges; where one overlaps 0 SD, the marker is hollow and the line turns grey." (uses the 90% range wording of COPY-10). Literal matches in tests: none for "(SD " or "±1 SD" (e2e/session.spec.ts:673/675 and run.test.ts:213 only mention SD in titles/comments).
